newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Stronger chemical production seen in 97-CEFIC.
newsitem.headline: Stronger chemical production seen in 97-CEFIC.

text.p: European chemicals production will be stronger in 1997, rising by over three percent, the European Chemical Industry Council (CEFIC) said on Wednesday.
It also said that initial indications of investment intentions suggested that the rise in capital spending was likely to be small, between two and three percent.
In a statement, CEFIC said 1997 would be relatively strong year for chemcials production, partly due to buoyant exports and changes in chemical stocks.
In 1996, chemicals production was set to increase by less than two percent. "The near-term outlook for the chemical industry in Europe has improved significantly compared with last year," CEFIC said.

"There is already evidence of an upward trend with output in the second half of 1996 growing at an annual rate of over five percent, a sharp rebound from the weak performance registered in the first six months," CEFIC said.
CEFIC also said that the fall in producer prices in Western Europe had to a "large degree" come to an end and that prices had either flattened out or were beginning to rise.
"For 1997, CEFIC predicts a rise in producer prices of one percent, with a strong possibility that the increase will be higher than projected," it said.
